about: Stars that pass through the Oort Cloud. The track is straight-line motion from the astrometry below (hand-entered, approximate); published closest approaches, which model the Galactic potential and the measurement errors, are quoted next to it.

stars.name: Gliese 710

astrometry.source: Gaia DR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2023), as used by Bailer-Jones (2022); hand-entered

published.source: de la Fuente Marcos & de la Fuente Marcos (2022, RNAAS 6, 136; Gaia DR3)

stars.description: An orange dwarf, now 62 light-years away in Serpens, heading almost straight at us at 14 km/s. In about 1.29 million years it will pass roughly 11,000-13,000 AU from the Sun, through the inner Oort Cloud, shining brighter than Jupiter. It is the closest stellar encounter known and should send a shower of comets inward over the following million years.

stars.name: Scholz's Star
stars.spectral: M9.5 + T5 (red dwarf and brown dwarf)

astrometry.source: Gaia DR3 parallax and proper motion; radial velocity from Burgasser et al. (2015, AJ 149, 104); hand-entered

stars.description: A dim red dwarf with a brown-dwarf companion, now 22 light-years away in Monoceros and receding at 83 km/s. About 70,000-80,000 years ago, while modern humans were spreading out of Africa, it grazed the outer Oort Cloud at roughly 50,000-70,000 AU. Even then it was too faint to see without a telescope.
